answers.answer: A Swift library for declarative command-line interfaces: property wrappers describe arguments/options/flags, parsing constructs a command, and command execution calls run() or reports help/errors. Swift CLI developers embed ArgumentParser; users launch their resulting executables. Repository examples include repeat, roll and math; the README also names swift-format and Swift Package Manager as adopters.

ArgumentParser owns the public command/property-wrapper API and parsing, validation, help and completion behavior. Internally CommandParser walks the command tree, LenientParser collects values, and ArgumentDecoder constructs the selected command. ArgumentParserToolInfo defines versioned Codable command/argument metadata. generate-manual and generate-docc-reference consume it to generate documentation; their SwiftPM command plugins invoke those tools. ArgumentParserTestHelpers supports the test targets, while Examples supplies runnable clients.

Implementation and examples are Swift; Package.swift uses Swift tools 6.0 and SwiftPM. One package exposes the ArgumentParser library and two plugin products, with separate internal ToolInfo/TestHelpers, executable and test targets; external package dependencies are empty. CMake is also supported: its project enables C and Swift (C is required for a GNUInstallDirs workaround), includes CTest, and adds Sources, optional Examples and Tests. Shell scripts provide ancillary tooling.

Examples/repeat/Repeat.swift declares @main struct Repeat: ParsableCommand. Its inherited static main() is the executable entry, delegating to main(nil); Repeat.run() is the command body. Package.swift declares executable target repeat at Examples/repeat.

The synchronous parse-then-run implementation is ParsableCommand.main(_ arguments: [String]?) in Sources/ArgumentParser/Parsable Types/ParsableCommand.swift, lines 148-165: it obtains a mutable command via parseAsRoot(arguments), calls try command.run(), and catches errors with exit(withError:). The zero-argument main() forwards nil; parseAsRoot creates CommandParser(self) and invokes its synchronous parse.

generate-manual directly depends on ArgumentParser and ArgumentParserToolInfo. Package.swift's executableTarget dependencies establish consumer -> dependency direction; GenerateManual.swift explicitly imports both and uses ParsableCommand plus decoded ToolInfoHeader/ToolInfoV0. Separately, GenerateManual (the plugin) depends on generate-manual, not the reverse. Foundation is imported but is not an internal package target.

Source-supported path for repeat hello: Repeat's @main -> inherited main() -> main(nil) -> parseAsRoot(nil), which drops argv[0] -> CommandParser.parse(arguments:) -> parseBesidesCustomCompletion -> SplitArguments -> descendingParse -> parseCurrent (LenientParser.parse, ArgumentDecoder, command-type init(from:)) -> validate -> selected command returned -> command.run(). Repeat has phrase='hello', count=nil, includeCounter=false; run uses count ?? 2 and prints hello twice. This is source reasoning, not a captured execution. Swift @main synthesis, protocol/metatype decoding and run dispatch cross compiler/dynamic boundaries; the map reports no call edges for main, so it does not prove a statically resolved end-to-end trace.

The five direct SwiftPM target consumers of ArgumentParserToolInfo are ArgumentParser, ArgumentParserTestHelpers, generate-docc-reference, generate-manual, and ArgumentParserToolInfoTests, evidenced by their own dependencies arrays. Other tests/examples/plugins may be transitively affected, but are not direct ToolInfo target dependencies in this manifest. This establishes declared dependency impact, not that every edit changes their runtime behavior.

RepeatExampleTests.repeatBasic() is a Swift Testing @Test that calls requireExecuteCommand(command: 'repeat hello') and expects two hello lines. The helper splits the command, resolves the built executable, passes the remaining arguments to Foundation.Process and launches it, thus entering Repeat's @main and the inherited synchronous parse-then-run path. The helper checks output and exit status. It returns without subprocess execution on Windows and unsupported Darwin platforms; I did not run the test.

OS arguments enter through Swift CommandLine.arguments, cached as CommandLine._staticArguments in Utilities/Platform.swift. parseAsRoot(nil) converts dropFirst() to [String], removing the executable name; a supplied explicit array bypasses that fallback and must already omit the command name. CommandParser receives that vector, checks custom-completion handling, then constructs SplitArguments before descending command parsing. SplitArguments preserves originalInput and tokenizes via parseIndividualArg into values, options and a -- terminator, retaining origin indexes; arguments after -- become values. For hello the token is a positional value.

limitations: No target execution or builds; runtime paths are source-supported deductions.
